stress.intro: We simulate {n} possible futures. In each one, these change at random:
stress.in.speed: How fast AI arrives: anywhere from Slow (half of Expected's change by 2030, our assumption) to Fast, most often close to Expected.
stress.in.estimate: How much AI can do each skill: our estimate plus or minus the error our exposure model makes on jobs it has never seen (typically 6.5 points out of 100). Half of that error is shared by all your skills.
stress.in.hours: Hours you really study: from half to one and a half times your {h} hours a week, most often as planned.
stress.in.weeks: Time each step takes: from 20% less to 20% more than our estimate.
stress.in.deadline: Your deadline stays as you set it.
stress.method: Your plan works in a future when three checks pass: no skill on your route is taken over by AI before you reach it, you are ready by your deadline (or the end of 2030), and the job is still in demand. This tests the plan, not your chance of being hired. The same plan always meets the same futures, so the number only changes when the plan does; it is accurate to within 2 to 3 points. Catalogue values are sample data.
